what_this_claim_does_not_cover: libssl and TLS: neither binary links libssl (DT_NEEDED is libcrypto only), so no SSL_CTX/SSL_SESSION/record-layer/handshake/renegotiation/certificate-chain-via-SSL behaviour is exercised. The 14 SSL_SESSION obligations the closure lists are reachable only through the monolithic candidate libcrypto's source-file mapping, not through an SSL import or the L7 workload.

workload generalisation: L7 is workload-specific. The evidence covers ssh-keygen Ed25519 sign/verify and sshd -D with a verified exec plus a host-key mismatch. It is not a claim about every use of openssh (no ciphers/kex matrix, rekeying, agent, multiplexing, sftp, certificates, FIDO, PAM, GSSAPI, Kerberos, port forwarding, or hostile-input protocol testing).
other consumers: only family:openssh and family:openssh-server. No other family, and none of the other 31 cohort families, inherits this evidence.

other mechanisms: the regenerated inventory has 80 production blockers crate-wide; only 14 are in the ssh upper bound and 13 in sshd. The other 66 are excluded as not in this linked set, not proven safe. Test-only and allocator-seam blockers are outside this closure.

reachability model: function-level static graph, not a whole-program proof. It admits 135 reachable unresolved indirect sites, 352 functions with unresolved indirect calls, 5242 address-taken candidates and 943 residual class entries; consumer-side dynamic name lookup is not modelled; two crate functions are unmapped; inlining is not represented. The L7 run attests the workload ran, not that it entered any particular site.

sanitizers and cryptographic assurance: no Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows), ASan, LSan, TSan, Loom, Kani, mutation, dudect, ctgrind or Wycheproof/ACVP court was run for this candidate/identity. Functional Ed25519 success is not a constant-time or vector-coverage result.

independent review and SEAL: no independent review of the openssh discharge, no full forensic regeneration, no full library suite at c7dc87ffb, no held-out/broad compatibility replay, and no release-candidate seal at this identity.
retained C-ABI obligation: a C-invalid pointer is outside the C contract at every exported pointer-taking entry point; that is retained, not discharged, and is not a claim about hostile C callers.
sibling legacy initialisers: sha256/384/512/512_224/512_256 and md5_sha1 keep the authority's unconditional md_data shape and are outside this closure.

reproducibility: the four install hashes are reproducible from this source in this container, but the consumer build's absolute path and the runtime build path affect the binary digests; the closure artifacts and the L7-executed binaries are not the same bytes.

independent_review.adjudicator_finding: REJECTED after independent re-derivation of the install, the ABI courts, the inventory, both consumer builds, both L7 workloads and both closures; the refusal and the uncontracted reachable sites are independently observed

non_claims: This file is an adjudication record, not a memory-safety proof.
A DISCHARGED value from consumer_closure.py means only that a committed receipt covers the exact site; it does not re-audit the receipt.
The 11 ABI courts are structural distribution-shell results, not semantic parity.
The L7 result is a workload-specific functional result, not a general openssh compatibility or cryptographic assurance claim.
